newsitem.title: USA: Downstream helps oil cos to beat market forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Downstream helps oil cos to beat market forecasts.

text.p: The top six U.S. oil companies have all reported earnings ahead of expectations as improved performance in refining and chemicals offset lower oil prices, but the rest of the year is not expected to show straight line growth.

On Wednesday, Mobil Corp, which also managed to improve from the year-ago quarter, USX-Marathon Group and Chevron Corp all illustrated the benefits of having downstream operations as a natural hedge against declining crude oil prices.

Mobil, the second largest U.S. oil company, had net income of $805 million, or $1.06 per share, including a $20 million charge for the startup of its European downstream venture with British Petroleum Co Plc, compared with $783 million a year ago, or $0.98 per share, including a $31 million charge.
Mobil said refining and marketing income rose to $420 million from $352 million, although that rise was dampened by plant shutdowns in Asia.
This more than offset a $0.94 per barrel fall in average crude oil prices to $16.18 per barrel here and a $2.16 fall overseas.

Income from operations, which reveals the true state of the business, rose seven percent to $870 million and Mobil's earnings per share from operations were $1.09, compared with forecasts of $1.01 and an actual $1.02 a year ago.

"Mobil's numbers were very good, but they were not the blowout that Exxon Corp had on Monday and the shares had risen in anticipation of higher earnings," said Eugene Nowak, analyst at ABN AMRO First Chicago Corp.
Mobil's stock fell 1-7/16 to 74-1/16 by early afternoon.
Like Exxon, Mobil's chemicals division improved with a $26 million rise in net income to $91 million.
Exxon had reported a 25 percent rise in net income.

USX-Marathon, the sixth largest oil company in the U.S. offset a 16 percent decline in upstream oil and natural gas earnings with a bumper 31 percent rise in refining and marketing earnings to $165 million before tax.
Its net income was $118 million, down from $124 million a year ago, but stripping out special items, the figure was $158 million, or $0.55 per share, way ahead of forecasts of $0.48 per share.
Last year the company earned $169 million, or $0.59 per share in the second quarter.
Fourth-ranked Chevron posted record second quarter operating earnings, up 20 percent at $700 million, despite a a fall in sales to $9.95 billion from $10.51 billion due to the fall in oil prices.
Net income fell to $823 million, or $1.26 a share, from $872, or $1.34 per share a year ago, beating analyst earnings per share forecasts of $1.10.

The dangers of dependency on drilling oil and natural gas alone without the benefit of a downstream hedge was illustrated by Unocal Corp, where operating income per share of $0.39 was way below analyst forecasts of $0.45 per share.

It was fully exposed to a seven percent fall in crude oil prices and total net income was almost half the level of the year ago quarter at $118 million, or $0.48 per share, compared with $238 million, or $0.92 per share.
Unocal stock rose 2/16 to 39-1/16 in early afternoon trading.
Looking forward to the rest of the year, analysts say that the improving trend of refining earnings is set to continue, but perhaps at a slower rate.
"This is going to remain a cyclical business, while there is good gasoline demand, there is no shortage of capacity and the jump we saw this quarter will not be repeated," said Nowak.

Chemicals too are a cyclical business and Salomon Brothers analyst Paul Ting notes that there is a huge amount of ethylene capacity being built which will come onstream next year and upset the demand and supply balance.
Among analysts' favourite picks, Exxon is one of Ting's because of its low debt to capitalisation ratio of 17 percent, which enables it to continue its share buyback.

Nowak's top pick is Texaco which trades on the lowest ratio of the majors and has cash to increase its dividend as well as what Nowak regards as the best production profile. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
